execution_steps: 1. Checked git log/status for concurrent-worker conflicts -- clean, no new commits since this session's own Event 352 commit (e9535447); 52 pre-existing unrelated dirty files confirmed untouched throughout this tick.

2. Reviewed Event 343's own named list of nrrd's remaining undocumented __all__ candidates (convert_endian, RoundingPolicy, axis_order_report/AxisOrderReport, flatten_nrrd_array, reshape_nrrd_array, dump_detached, decode_nrrd_data/encode_nrrd_data, load_nrrd/probe_nrrd/write_nrrd) and investigated the axis-order/shape-conversion cluster first, since flatten_nrrd_array/reshape_nrrd_array/axis_order_report were all added together this same session (Events 328-331) and looked most likely to form one cohesive, closeable capability rather than isolated cosmetic gaps.

3. Read model/document.py's NrrdDocument.to_array() (line 501) and confirmed it is exactly what get_array() (already documented in the README) calls -- reshape_nrrd_array(self.array, self.sizes) -- so the README's existing read-side example was already accurate and complete. Read with_array() (line 504) immediately after and confirmed it is the real, symmetric, tested WRITE-side counterpart: flatten_nrrd_array(nested, self.sizes), returning a new NrrdDocument with the payload replaced -- genuinely undocumented despite being a real capability that completes an already-partially-documented pair, not a supporting type.

4. Read axis_order_report()/AxisOrderReport in full (lines 515-557): confirmed it returns the exact same sizes/strides/nesting_order mapping to_array()/with_array() use internally, callable independently of any array's own values -- useful for a caller who wants to know which NRRD axis a given nesting depth corresponds to without performing a conversion. Judged this a natural, small addition to the same section rather than its own separate slice, since it directly explains the mapping the new with_array() example already uses.

5. Verified the exact example before writing it: loaded samples/by-format/nrrd/valid/2d-float32.nrrd, called get_array() (matches existing README claim), built a doubled host-order array, called document.with_array() on it, dumped the result to a real temp file, reloaded it, and confirmed the reloaded array matched the doubled values exactly -- a genuine disk round trip, not merely an in-memory check. Called axis_order_report(edited.sizes) and got strides=(1,2)/nesting_order=(1,0).

6. Caught a real mistake mid-verification: a first draft of the README example used `document.header['sizes']` as axis_order_report()'s own argument -- direct execution showed this is the RAW, unparsed header string ('2 3'), not the parsed list axis_order_report() expects, which would have silently produced wrong output (iterating over a 3-character string as a 'sizes' list) rather than raising. Corrected to the parsed `document.sizes` property before publishing, and disclosed the near-miss directly in the documentation-gate.json's own evidence rather than silently fixing it.
